description: A sensation of difficulty breathing, not getting enough air, or breathing that feels harder or faster than normal.

child_flow.question: Has your child been diagnosed with asthma or reactive airway disease?
Has your child recently had a cold, flu, RSV, or pneumonia?
Was your child recently exposed to allergens, smoke, or anything that triggers wheezing?
Does your child have sickle cell disease?
Is your child struggling to breathe, wheezing, or unable to speak full sentences?
When did the breathing difficulty start?

adult_flow.question: What is your biological sex?
Are you pregnant or have you recently given birth?
When did the shortness of breath start?
Are you also experiencing chest pain or pressure?
Did the breathing difficulty come on suddenly?
Describe your main breathing difficulty (tight chest, fast breathing, wheezing, gasping).
Has your breathing been getting better, worse, or staying the same?
Are you short of breath while resting, or only when walking or climbing stairs?
Can you speak in full sentences without needing to stop for breath?
Are you feeling faint, lightheaded, or confused?
Have you noticed your lips or fingertips turning blue or grey?
Do you have a cough?
If coughing, what colour is the mucus?
Are you wheezing or making a whistling sound when breathing?
Do you have a history of asthma, COPD, heart disease, anemia, or blood clots?
Have you recently had surgery, long travel, or bed rest for several days?
Are you currently on hormone therapy (birth control pills, hormone replacement)?
Do you have a history of blood clots or deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?
Do you take inhalers, blood thinners, hormone therapy, or any regular medications?
Did this begin after exposure to something you’re allergic to (food, medication, insect sting)?
Has this happened before? If yes, what was the cause?

red_flags: Shortness of breath that is getting worse or not improving with rest
Shortness of breath at rest or when speaking a few words
Inability to speak full sentences without stopping for breath
Blue or grey color of the lips, face, or fingertips
Chest pain or pressure together with shortness of breath
Feeling of suffocating or air hunger
Severe wheezing or very noisy breathing
Breathing that is much faster or more shallow than usual
New confusion, extreme fatigue, or feeling like you might faint
Very fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat with breathlessness
Swelling or pain in one leg together with shortness of breath
Shortness of breath with high fever, shaking chills, or feeling very unwell
safety_disclaimer: This information is for general education only and does not replace a medical assessment.
